steps.title: What this tab is for
steps.body: This tab runs an automated opponent that paces your solo or cooperative game. It never plays on the board for you — each turn it tells you what the opponent does, and you carry that out at the table.

steps.title: First: Volkare or a Knight
steps.body: Choose Volkare — the Lost Legion antagonist, who has no Knight — or a Knight you aren't playing, which stands in as the opponent.

steps.title: Then: Standard or Proxy
steps.body: If you picked a Knight, choose how richly to run it. Standard Dummy Player just flips cards to keep the game moving. Proxy Player (from Apocalypse Dragon) is a fuller opponent that chases objectives around the map.

steps.title: Set the options and Start
steps.body: Toggle Cooperative play and whether the game starts at night, then tap Start. Use whichever mode your scenario calls for — exactly one per game.

steps.title: Resuming a game
steps.body: The app autosaves after every action, so you can close it mid-game. Next time, the Restore Game button on this screen picks up exactly where you left off — deck, round, and log intact.

steps.title: A pacing opponent
steps.body: The Dummy Player is a stand-in that races you through the rounds. It never fights or moves on the map — watching its deck shrink is how you gauge how much time you have left.

steps.title: Tactics each round
steps.body: Each round opens with a Tactic draft for turn order. Pick your card in the popup — the app applies the correct pick order and Tactic removal for your specific scenario, so you never have to look those rules up.

steps.title: Play Turn
steps.body: Each turn it flips 3 cards, then checks the 3rd card's colour and flips one extra card per crystal it holds of that colour. Tap Play Turn and the app does all of this for you.

steps.title: Ending and preparing a round
steps.body: When its deck runs empty it announces End of the Round — everyone takes one last turn, then tap End Round. At round end it gains the lowest Advanced Action from the offer and reshuffles its deck; the dialog just asks which offer cards came up.

steps.title: Undo anything
steps.body: Tapped the wrong thing? The undo arrow at the bottom-left reverts your last action, so mistakes are cheap.

steps.title: Why the deck count matters
steps.body: Some scenarios (such as Solo Conquest) score you on how many cards are left in the Dummy Player's deck at the end — so keep an eye on the count in the header.

steps.title: A richer opponent
steps.body: The Proxy Player, from Apocalypse Dragon, replaces the Dummy Player with a Hero that chases objectives around the map. As with Volkare, the app narrates what it does; you resolve the real movement and combat at the table.

steps.title: Tactics each round
steps.body: Each round opens with a Tactic draft for turn order. Pick your card in the popup — the app applies the pick order and Tactic removal your scenario uses, so you don't have to track them.

steps.title: Objective cards
steps.body: Each turn it works toward an Objective Card drawn from its deck. The colour tells you its target: green heads for an adventure site, red for a fortified site or monastery, white for recruiting or learning, and blue for any of those but further from the portal.

steps.title: Play Turn
steps.body: Tap Play Turn: if it already has an objective it adds a Shield token and flips 3 cards; otherwise it draws a new objective and flips 2 more. Crystals matching the last card's colour flip extra cards, just like the Dummy Player.

steps.title: Movement points
steps.body: The app totals the objective's movement points for you — from the card type, its Shield tokens, and a Source-die bonus (including the gold die on days). Move the Hero that many spaces toward its target.

steps.title: Report the result — and undo
steps.body: After you resolve it at the table, tell the app: still travelling (keep the objective) or resolved — Explored or Completed. Made a wrong tap anywhere? The undo arrow at the bottom-left reverts your last action.

steps.title: The Lost Legion antagonist
steps.body: Volkare replaces the Dummy Player in Volkare's Return and Volkare's Quest, racing you across the map. The app narrates each card he reveals; you move his figure and resolve any fight at the table.

steps.title: Tactics each round
steps.body: Each round opens with a Tactic draft for turn order. The app applies the right rules for you — including Volkare's own quirk that in cooperative play the real players pick first, unlike every other scenario.

steps.title: One card per turn
steps.body: Volkare's deck is dealt once and never reshuffled. Each turn reveals a single card — tap the button and the app tells you what it means: which way he moves, whether the Source die rerolls, or whether he attacks.

steps.title: City Revealed (Return only)
steps.body: In Volkare's Return, flip the City Revealed switch once the city tile appears on the board. Before it's set, moves are narrated as fixed compass directions; after, as moving toward the city.

steps.title: Deck's end — and undo
steps.body: In Volkare's Return an empty deck triggers Frenzy: every turn afterward is a double move, forever. In Volkare's Quest, his last move card means he reached the portal and you've lost the race. Tapped wrong? The undo arrow reverts your last action.

steps.title: Replaces the token piles
steps.body: This tab stands in for the physical face-down enemy, ruin, and faction token piles. It's the real source of what each pile holds and what's been drawn, so it saves your progress for the whole game.

steps.title: Drawing a token
steps.body: Tap a pile to draw from it — use the stepper to draw several at once. The token appears zoomed, and its "?" window explains any abilities. It's discarded immediately: the app tracks no map and no combat, just the draw.

steps.title: The Draw Log is your board memory
steps.body: Every draw is recorded in the Draw Log, newest first. Because the app models no board, this log is your only record of which enemies are still standing on which spaces — treat it as your memory of the table.

steps.title: Marking defeats
steps.body: Tap a log entry and mark it Defeated once you beat it. Undefeated tokens stay "on the board" at the top; defeated ones drop into the pile's discard and are reshuffled back only once that pile runs out.

steps.title: Choosing your tokens
steps.body: The config section sets the Token Set (which expansions' tokens are in play) and an optional Draw with Replacement. Changing these rebuilds the piles and clears the log, so they only take effect when you tap Apply & Reset.

steps.title: Surveying a pile
steps.body: Tap a pile's count line to see which tokens remain — grouped by type, with counts, but never in draw order — handy for weighing your odds before you commit to a fight.
